sentences.text: Boats with gasoline engines in enclosed spaces must have ventilation to remove explosive vapor, usually natural vents plus a powered blower.
Run the blower for at least four minutes before starting the engine, and sniff the bilge.

Gasoline inboard and sterndrive engines must have a Coast Guard approved backfire flame arrestor on the carburetor or throttle body, kept clean and firmly secured, so a backfire can’t ignite vapor in the compartment.
Diesel engines are far less explosive, but their spaces still need ventilation to supply combustion air.
